title: pocket-conference-and-papers-scrap-2026-12-09
content:
Quick pocket notes from a handful of papers and talks I skimmed over the last week + actionable experiments to try. This is messy — brain dump for follow-up.

Context:
- Running through a few systems papers on KV-cache compression, prefix caching tradeoffs, and micro-batching kernels. Thinking about what we can prototype on Dedicated in Jan (small-scale perf tests) before proposing any Optimize UI knobs.
- Main constraints: keep 99p latency SLO, avoid regressions on rare long-tail sequences, keep e2e noise low when comparing quantized kernels.

Paper / talk snippets (very condensed):
1) "Compact KV via locality-aware chunking" (poster)
- Idea: chunk KV pairs by local context similarity (L2 on projected keys) and compress per-chunk with lightweight quantization + tiny index.
- Observed: 2.5x token throughput improvement when working set fits compressed chunks in GPU L2; 10–20% latency win for 8k context models on 80/20 workloads.
- My take: promising for customers with skewed context (single-doc sessions). Risk: additional CPU/GPU preproc for chunking.
- Quick experiment: run end-to-end on small 1-GPU Dedicated instance using our KV shim + fake workload (doc-heavy chat). Measure latency tail and extra CPU cycles for chunking. Ticket: link above PR/3021 might be relevant.

2) "Adaptive prefix eviction with prediction head" (oral)
- Use a tiny predictor (MLP) to predict future reuse of prefixes; evict low-score prefixes proactively to avoid kvcache blowups.
- Nice results on simulated workloads (less cache thrash -> better tail latency).
- Concern: predictor overhead and risk of evicting soon-to-be-used prefixes in multi-turn assistants.
- Experiment idea: implement as an opt-in policy in private infra; compare FIFO vs predictor vs LRU on replay logs (sampled).

3) "Kernel fusion and late-binding quant kernels" (systems talk)
- Runtime picks between fused kernels at dispatch time based on sequence length and quant profile. Late-binding lets you keep one model artifact and pick faster kernels dynamically.
- This aligns with our compilation+kernel-selection story; gap is infra for fast per-request decision-making.
- TODO: sketch a policy proto that maps (model variant, seq_len_bucket, quant_profile) -> kernel_choice and evaluate scheduling overhead. Put a 50us budget on decision path.

Conference takeaways (operations/strategy):
- People care about predictable tail more than average throughput. Marketing angle: predictability + cost controls.
- Several teams asked about multi-tenant shared kvcache safety — suggests we should write a short public note about "kvcache locality and tenant isolation" (small doc).
- Benchmarks still inconsistent across papers — need to publish our micro-bench harness for kv/cache experiments so comparisons are reproducible.

Actionable experiments (short-term, small scope):
- E1: KV-chunk compression prototype on 1xA10 Dedicated (measured): implement chunking transform in C++ shim + quantize to 4-bit per-chunk, run replay of 10k sessions from logs. Measure: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, extra CPU % on preproc. Owner: Kiara. ETA: 2027-01-20. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infer/pull/3021 (wip).
- E2: LRU vs predictor eviction replay test: build predictor offline from logs (small MLP in PyTorch), run policy in simulator to measure hit-rate and latency impact. Owner: Owen. ETA: 2027-01-12. Save model to experiments/kvcache/predictor-v1.pt.
- E3: Kernel decision policy microbenchmark: add decision layer in runtime that picks kernel in <50us. Use synthetic seq_len distribution (from prod hist) to measure overhead. Owner: SRE pair with runtime eng. ETA: 2026-12-23 (fast spike).

Open questions / risks:
- How do compressed-chunk indices behave under eviction/migration? We need a plan for fast rehydration of compressed chunks when evicted. Potential approach: keep tiny CSV index in CPU memory and stream decompress on miss — cost estimate unknown.
- Quantization stability: which layers degrade output quality most? We should add a small automatic eval (QA-style prompts) to catch early quality regressions when testing 4-bit chunk compression. This ties into Optimize quality monitors.
- Can we expose chunking/predictor as pluggable policies for Private customers? If so we need API design and docs.

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Ping @Avery about schedule for using a spare Dedicated slot in Jan. (Slack thread referenced in linked_artifacts.)
- Draft quick public note about kvcache locality and tenant isolation (1 pager) — aim to publish Feb.
- Add micro-benchmark harness to repo and CI (flake: needs GPU access gating). Create GH issue to track infra work (owner: Kiara).

Random crumbs I liked / want to re-read:
- microblog link: https://notes.example/podcasts/kv-compress (short writeup, practical tips)
- blog: "practical prefix batching" — has a small code snippet that might slot into our runtime with minimal changes. Save snippet to snippets/prefix-batching.txt.

Immediate todo (today):
- create GH issue for E1 + attach minimal design sketch (2 paragraphs)
- send quick calendar invite for 30m sync with Owen + Avery to align on replay dataset
- stash this doc in users and mark as reference when writing proposal for Optimize experiments

End of dump. Will tidy into a PR-ready doc after the Jan spike and first experiment results.
